name: Naproxen
drug_class: Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (propionic acid derivative, non-selective COX inhibitor)
route_note: Oral tablets, controlled-release tablets and suspension, usually twice daily; suppositories in some countries.

discovery.note: Developed by Syntex in the late 1960s; marketed as the single S-enantiomer. Year is the first patent filing.

rx_status: OTC at low doses (naproxen sodium); prescription at higher doses
tagline: Long-acting NSAID used twice daily for arthritis and pain
summary: Naproxen is a long-acting non-selective NSAID developed by Syntex and used for arthritis, musculoskeletal pain, dysmenorrhoea and gout. Its longer half-life allows twice-daily dosing, and some studies suggest a comparatively lower cardiovascular risk than other NSAIDs.
mechanism: Naproxen reversibly inhibits COX-1 and COX-2, reducing prostaglandin synthesis and thereby inflammation, pain and fever.

At regular full doses its sustained COX-1 inhibition in platelets produces a more aspirin-like antiplatelet effect than shorter-acting NSAIDs, which has been suggested to explain its relatively neutral cardiovascular profile in some analyses.
uses: Rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis and ankylosing spondylitis

history.title: Over the counter
history.detail: Naproxen sodium is approved for non-prescription sale in the US as Aleve.

history.title: VIGOR
history.detail: In the VIGOR trial, rofecoxib causes more myocardial infarctions than naproxen, feeding debate over COX-2 inhibitors.

history.title: NSAID boxed warning
history.detail: Prescription NSAIDs, including naproxen, receive FDA cardiovascular and gastrointestinal boxed warnings.

history.title: Vimovo
history.detail: A fixed combination of naproxen with esomeprazole is approved to reduce gastric ulcer risk.

history.title: PRECISION
history.detail: In the PRECISION trial, cardiovascular safety of naproxen is similar to that of celecoxib and ibuprofen at moderate doses.

pk.metabolism: hepatic, CYP2C9 and CYP1A2 to 6-desmethylnaproxen, and glucuronidation

safety.boxed_warning: Cardiovascular thrombotic events (myocardial infarction, stroke) and serious gastrointestinal bleeding, ulceration and perforation; contraindicated for pain after coronary artery bypass graft surgery (US NSAID class boxed warning).

facts: Naproxen is marketed as a single (S)-enantiomer, unlike ibuprofen, which is sold as a racemic mixture.
